# Praelecta

> AI lecture recording and study tool for university students. Record the lecture; a few minutes after class it is a transcript, a summary and flashcards, with practice questions on paid plans. Tick which lectures a test covers, and on the Scholar plan the study sessions are booked around your calendar. Made in Canada, priced in CAD, billed by the semester.

Praelecta is built for undergraduate students in content-heavy courses (engineering, sciences, math) who would rather not redo the whole course at exam time. It is a web app (praelecta.ca) with desktop apps for Mac, Windows and Linux; an iPhone app is on the way.

What it does:
- Records a lecture (up to six hours) after the student confirms they have permission, then transcribes it (Groq; Deepgram as a fallback) and writes the summary, key concepts, formulas, definitions, worked examples, exam mentions and to-dos (Google Gemini).
- Attaches the professor's files (slides, syllabus, formula sheets, past exams) to a lecture or a course; formulas are verified against them, and practice material can be built from them.
- Lets the student tick which lectures a test covers, so flashcards, practice questions, quizzes and class handbooks stay inside that slice.
- Books study sessions between now and the exam around the student's classes and work shifts (Scholar plan), rebooks a missed one when asked, and runs a focus timer with an end-of-session review.
- Imports a class timetable from a photo or PDF to set up the semester.

Pricing (CAD): two full lectures of up to 90 minutes free (30 credits), no card. Student $7.99/month or $24.99/semester (200 credits a month, about 20 hours of lectures); Scholar $12.99/month or $39.99/semester (450 credits); Unlimited $24.99/month or $79.99/semester (1000 credits). A one-hour lecture costs 10 credits. Credit packs (100 for $6.99, 250 for $14.99, 500 for $27.99) never expire. Students cancel themselves in Settings; the price you sign up at never rises while you stay subscribed.

Commitments: recordings run up to six hours and survive a browser crash; every limit is visible before you hit it; students cancel themselves in Settings; the app helps with lectures, never with writing assignments. Recordings are private to the student's account and are deleted when they delete them. Analytics runs only for visitors who allow it.
